# Read-back: Breakfast for Six on One Griddle

A complete breakfast—pancakes, bacon, scrambled eggs, toast, and fresh coffee—is being prepared for six people by one cook, with all components ready to serve together by 09:00. The griddle is the primary constraint: it must heat, cook bacon, be cleaned, then cook three sequential passes of pancakes, cool to a lower temperature, and finally scramble eggs—all on one electric surface. Supporting equipment includes one two-slice toaster (which runs two batches sequentially), one coffee maker with a burner grinder, and one oven at its lowest setting used only to hold six warm plates and to store finished components (bacon, pancake passes) while other work continues. The timeline is tightly choreographed: pancake batter must rest for 20 minutes after mixing; eggs must be beaten and set aside; the table must be laid; and toast must be buttered. The coffee grinder is timed to start ten minutes after bacon finishes, so the pot is fresh at serve time. Everything—eggs, toast, and coffee—must finish at the same moment so the cook can call everyone to eat and carry the warm plates from the oven.
